25 March, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Jbp:24590

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Jabalpur
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice B. P. Sharma

On The 25th Of March, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 50097 of 2024
 Bhupendra Kumar Paraste
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Mrs. Anchan Pandey - Advocate with Shri Mansih Kumar M
 Advocate for the petitioner.
 Shri Himanshu Soni - Panel Lawyer for respondent No.1 
 Shri Rajeshwar Dixit - Advocate for objector.
 Order

This petition under Section 482 of CrPC, 1973 (Section 528 of BNSS, 2023) has been filed by the petitioner seeking quashment of FIR bearing Crime No. 383/2023 dated 30.9.2023 registered at Police Station Bichhiya, District Mandla (M.P.), for the offence punishable under Sections 363,
366A, 376, and 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5L,6 of the POCSO Act as well as quashment of all consequential proceedings arising therefrom including the proceedings in SC No.45/2024 (State of MP Vs. Bhupendra Kumar Paraste) pending before the Trial Court at Mandla.

sentences.text:
2 . Brief facts giving rise to the present petition are that according to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:24590 2 MCRC-50097-2024 the prosecution, on 30.9.2023 the complainant Seema Mandal had lodged FIR No.383/2023 regarding missing of her minor daughter Dipika Mandal aged about 18 years and 3 months.
3 Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner is innocent and he has falsely been implicated in this case.
The prosecutrix and applicant have entered into wedlock on 25.6.2024.
It is further submitted that in the present case, the parties have amicably settled the dispute by way of compromise, which has been duly verified.
Offences do not effect society at large and offences are primarily economic in nature.

It is, therefore, prayed that FIR bearing Crime No.383 dated 30.9.2023 registered at Police Station Bichiya, District Mandla (M.P.), for the offence punishable Bhupendra Kumar Paraste vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107517974/
1 under Sections 363, 366A, 376, and 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5L,6 of the POCSO Act as well as all consequential proceedings arising therefrom including the proceedings inSC No.45/2024 pending before the Special Judge, POCSO Act, District Mandla be quashed.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that as per the missing person report, the age of the prosecutrix was 18 years and 3 months at the time of incident.
She was major at the time of incident.
Petitioner and the prosecutrix married to each other and they are living together as husband and wife.

Therefore, in view of the judgments of Delhi High Court passed in case of Arjun Kamti Vs. The State of GNCT of Delhi through SHO & Ors (Crl.M.C.5323/2023 & Crl.M.A.20227/2023) as well as Allahabad High Court in case of Rajiv Kumar Vs. State of U.P. and 2 others (Application U/S 482 No.-4392 of 2016), the FIR and the subsequent proceedings based thereon may be quashed.

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:24590 3 MCRC-50097-2024 4 .
Learned counsel for the State as well as learned counsel appearing for the objector opposes the petition.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
6 .

Vide order dated 03.12.2024, this Court had directed the Registrar (J-II) of this Court for recording the statement of the parties for compromise and for verification of compromise arrived at between the parties.
In compliance whereof, Registrar (J-II) has submitted report dated 11.12.2024 accompanied by compromise entered between the parties.

Along with the report, statements of the parties with regard to compromise are also attached stating therein that parties have arrived at a compromise on their free will & volition and without any threat, inducement or coercion to settle their dispute and the compromise is voluntarily.
Petitioner and victim have been duly identified by the counsel.
Both petitioner and victim are major and entered into wedlock in the year 2024 and they are residing happily together.
7. Evidently, parties have entered into a compromise, which has been duly verified by Registrar (J-II) of this Court.

Hence, in view of compromise between the parties and in view of law laid down by the three -Judge Bench of Hon'ble Apex Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi and Others Vs. Babita Raghuvanshi and Another (2013) 4 SCC 58 so also the judgment of the Rajasthan High Court in case of Tarun Vaishanav Vs. State of Rajasthan reported in 2022 SCC OnLine Raj 2237, in which the Court has quashed the offence, entertained the petition under Section 482 of CrPC and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:24590 4 MCRC-50097-2024 that order of Rajasthan High Court was affirmed by the Supreme Court in Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No.1890/2023 parties being The State of Rajasthan Vs. Tarun Vishnav & Anr., dismissing the appeal of the State vide order dated 03.03.2023, the present petition filed by the petitioner deserves to be allowed.
